title: The nest no longer leans west
question: The fixed nest spreads its galleries down both sides of the door. Does it read better, the same, or worse than today’s one-sided nest?
context_md:
**What changed.** An ant already underground turns one step toward straight down before it digs (shipped 2026-09-28). An ant facing straight *up* has no shorter way round, and the rule always took the same side, so every such digger came down through the west. The other lane's review found it; now each such turn takes either side by a coin of its own.

**What it did to the nest** (dig box, 40 ants, 24 seeds, frame 24,000):

| | today | this change |
|---|---:|---:|
| nest leans west of the door (seeds) | **24 of 24** | 22 of 24 |
| median lean, columns | -11 | -8 |
| dug cells standing (median) | 207.5 | 260 (more on 20 of 24) |
| entrances (median) | 6.5 | 6 |
| turns down booked (sum) | 16,188 | 16,829 |

**Most of the lean that is left is the storeroom**, which the founding cuts on the west side: the founding cut alone reads -5. With the storeroom off, today's nest leans west on 19 of 24 and the fixed one on 10 (12 east, median +0.5). At 200 ants: west on 21 of 24 today, 15 with the change.

Also in this PR, invisible here: the founding cut leaves a corpse where it lies (it used to delete it, and its food value with it), and a species founds with its own jaw (a beetle colony used to dig the ants' shaft). Colony bed: born 179 -> 188, starved 82 -> 57.
